description: Build a shell script of raidcom commands from steps. Each step is a command with options, optionally repeated with `foreach` (every combination) or `zip` (values advance together), so "create LDEVs 100 to 109 in pool 0, then map each to port CL1-A" is two steps. Every expanded command is validated; the script is returned only if all of them are valid, otherwise you get the errors per step. The script checks each command's exit status, adds `raidcom get command_status` after asynchronous commands, and can lock the resource group and log in (credentials are read from RAIDCOM_USER and RAIDCOM_PASSWORD in the user's shell, never written into the script). Nothing is executed.

description.description: A one-line comment for the top of the script.

global.description: Settings that apply to the whole command, not to one raidcom option.

checkmode.description: Check the command without changing the array (-checkmode precheck).

instance.description: CCI instance number: written as -I<n>. Example: 0.

pair_type.description: With instance: H or TC for TrueCopy, Universal Replicator and global-active device; M or SI for ShadowImage, Volume Migration and Thin Image.

serial.description: Storage system serial number (-s), needed when the HORCM file lists several arrays. VSP 5000 series add a leading 5, VSP G1x00 and VSP F1500 a leading 3.

store.description: File name for the implementation-check file (-store).

unit.description: Unit ID of the command device (-u).

lock_resource.description: Wrap the commands in raidcom lock resource / unlock resource. Recommended for changing commands.

model.description: Storage model, so values are checked against its limits: vsp-one-b24, vsp-one-b26, vsp-one-b28, vsp-5000, vsp-e590, vsp-e790, vsp-e990, vsp-e1090. Aliases such as B28 or E990 work. Omit it to check against the widest range of any model.

foreach.description: Repeat the step for every value (cartesian product when there are several variables). Variable → list or range: {"ldev": "100-109"} or {"port": ["CL1-A", "CL2-A"]}. Reference a variable in option values as {ldev}. Example: options {"-ldev_id": "{ldev}"} with foreach {"ldev": "100-109"} writes ten commands.

options.description: raidcom options and their values, keyed by option name with or without the leading dash. A value is a string or number; an option that takes several values (for example -port takes a port and an optional host group name) takes an array: {"-port": ["CL1-A-0", "esx01"]}. An option with no value (a switch such as -allports) is true. Example for `add lun`: {"-port": ["CL1-A-0"], "-ldev_id": 200, "-lun_id": 1}.

title.description: A short label, written into the script as a comment.

zip.description: Like foreach, but the variables advance together and the lists must have the same length: {"ldev": "100-103", "lun": "0-3"} pairs LDEV 100 with LUN 0, 101 with 1, and so on.

strict.description: Default true. The command catalogue is parsed from the manual, whose syntax lines are occasionally incomplete, so a "needs <option>" error can be a false alarm. If one looks wrong after reading raidcom_describe_command, retry with strict=false: missing-option errors then become warnings. Unknown options and out-of-range values stay errors.

name: raidcom_build_script
title: Build a raidcom script
